guitar.evidence: John Frusciante's vintage Fender Stratocasters (and some Telecasters/Jaguars) are well documented across the band's biggest albums (Californication, By the Way).

tone.target: dry punk-funk clean crunch with bright wah bite
tone.profile: dry punk-funk clean crunch with bright wah bite
tone.summary: A tight signal chain utilizing a Boost/OD for initial grit, followed by a classic Fender-style amp (US Deluxe) paired with a small cab. Wah is placed early to shape the tone dynamically, maintaining dryness throughout.

rig.name: Red Hot Chili Peppers - Give It Away - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray hum and pick noise for tight punk rhythm playing.
Provide the bright nasal wah bite essential for funk/punk rhythm accents.
Add controlled clean-to-edge breakup and percussive punch without heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD 9/Green OD to keep the tone cleaner and more focused on transient attack.

alternatives.reason: A slightly dirtier alternative if more grit is desired.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, clean Fender-style amp tone required for funk/punk.
Provide a small, focused cabinet sound that complements the clean US Deluxe tone.
Fine-tune the frequency response to emphasize brightness and cut low-end mud, maintaining dryness.
Optional subtle thickening for sustained notes, but kept off to maintain dryness.
blocks.gap: The Chorus is generally avoided per the 'avoid' list (thick chorus), so it is set inactive. It remains as a potential texture module.

blocks.purpose: Provide a minimal, dry low-ambient mix without sounding like heavy reverb.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and tonal focus by swapping the default IR for a more focused, bright punk/funk cab.

proposals.reason: Enhance percussive clarity and brightness needed for funk-punk genre.
